$comment: TEMPLATE -- this file ships with the product and must never contain a
real address, file path, or username. To configure a second computer:
copy this file to config/machines.profile.json (already gitignored, so
your copy is never committed), fill it in with YOUR values, and set
"mode" to "multi". If you never create that copy at all, this program
works as a normal single-machine install with zero setup -- absence of a
profile is the common case, not an error.
$comment_mode: "single" (default) if you only ever use this on one computer. "multi" once you have listed at least one real entry under "peers" below.
$comment_transport: One of: "direct" (free, works only when your computers already share a network), "self-hosted-relay" (free, works from anywhere, you run and secure the relay server yourself), "hosted-relay" (paid, works from anywhere, nothing for you to run).
$comment_this_machine: "id" is a short lowercase slug YOU choose to name this computer -- letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore only, e.g. "desktop" or "work-laptop". It is deliberately not an IP address and not a file path, so it keeps working if your network address changes or you move this folder to a new location. "label" is only what you see on screen.
$comment_peers: Each entry describes one OTHER computer you own, for example: { "id": "laptop", "label": "My laptop", "address": "how-to-reach-it", "root": "where the checkout lives on that machine" }. Add an entry here and set "mode" above to "multi" to turn on cross-machine features. An entry cannot name itself as its own peer, and its "id" must be a valid slug like the one you chose for thisMachine.id above -- anything else is ignored and reported rather than guessed at.
